key_insight: A compactly supported hat-function kinetic model can capture contact discontinuities while preserving positivity, offering a simpler alternative to Maxwellian-based Boltzmann schemes.
engineering_relevance: The method provides a positivity-preserving first-order solver and a second-order extension for inviscid gas dynamics, making it attractive for robust CFD on shocks and contact waves.
method: Replace the Maxwellian velocity distribution with Perthame’s compact hat function in a Boltzmann-type formulation.
Use peculiar velocity moments to recover Euler conserved variables and fluxes.
Extend the scheme to second order while retaining the first-order positivity property.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports testing on several benchmark inviscid flow problems in one and two dimensions, with analysis that directly proves positivity due to compact velocity support.
watch_item: Performance claims are based on benchmark inviscid cases, so behavior on strongly multidimensional or highly complex flows may need additional validation.
paper_title: A hat function based positive contact discontinuity capturing Boltzmann scheme
